Very dear and greatly beloved mother and lady. Through my faithful chamberlain Enagut the Fleming, I received a few days ago with joy your honorable and gracious letters, to which I have not been able to respond until now because the lord king, my very dear lord and husband, has been gravely ill with double tertian fever, to such an extent that his illness was very doubtful [i.e., his recovery was uncertain], and he could not recover. And because of this, all affairs ceased. And this, by the grace of our lord God, may be praised, for he is now beyond the worst, according to the opinion of the physicians, and in great hope and anxious watchfulness, [expecting recovery] shortly.

Furthermore, my lady, I have very great pleasure in part, [knowing] that my lord father and lord, and my very dear brothers are [well]. May it please divine clemency that, if ever it were so, [they] may continue long in accordance with [their] desires, as we wish.

And because, my very dear mother and lady, [you wish] to know of my good estate, we inform you that I and the Infante Don Fernando, my firstborn, and the Infanta Doña Yolant, my daughter, your grandchildren, are healthy and in good disposition of our persons.

[I] beg you, very dear mother, that you would inform me of the health and estate of the lord duke, my very dear father and lord, and of my dear brothers, and all the matters relating to [your affairs] there, as is fitting, and [know] that you are held with continual and firm desire, and in which [we take] true, supreme, and full pleasure.

As for the cloths of velvet and other jewels that you request from my chamberlain, [I cannot send them now] and I cannot tell you [when], for the reason that there is no stock of them here, nor of such [goods], and I would wish to send [them] to you. But within a short time, some ships are due to arrive in Barcelona which are supposed to bring [such goods], and then I shall send [them] to you promptly. Here I can send you some of the jewels you request, [whether] for purchase or otherwise, only [what is available] from some places with the means at hand, to send to you, my lady.

## 4. HISTORICAL NOTES

### Persons

**B. Bardinus / Bernardus Bardinus**: Apostolic nuncio mentioned as having traveled from the Papal court at Avignon to the Crown of Aragon. This individual was likely involved in diplomatic negotiations concerning the Western Schism, during which the Crown of Aragon supported Clement VII at Avignon.

**Bishop of Couserans (Cousanen[sis] Episcopus)**: The Bishop of Couserans (modern Saint-Lizier in the French Pyrenees). In 1389, this was likely **Pierre Roger de Beaufort** or his successor. Couserans was a small Pyrenean diocese on the French side, often involved in Franco-Aragonese ecclesiastical diplomacy.

**Brother Simon Mathei**: A member of the Order of St. John of Jerusalem (Knights Hospitaller), serving as preceptor of a commandery. He acted as messenger between Queen Violant and her mother.

**Marie de France, Duchess of Bar**: Violant de Bar's mother, daughter of King Jean II of France. She married Robert I, Duke of Bar. The "egregia comitissa mater carissima" salutation reflects both familial affection and her ducal status (though "comitissa" is used, likely honorifically or due to scribal convention).

### Places

**Monzón (Montissoni)**: Town in Aragon where the Corts (parliamentary assembly) were frequently held. King Joan I and Queen Violant were present there in August 1389, conducting royal and diplomatic business during parliamentary sessions.

### Context

**Date Confirmation**: The documents date to 1 August 1389. The previous folio shows a document dated 22 August 1388, indicating the register is not strictly chronological within each year, or these represent a new sequence of entries. The year "M ccc lxxx viiij" (1389) is clearly within the register's 1387-1390 range.

**Western Schism Context**: These letters of credence relate to ongoing diplomatic communications during the Western Schism (1378-1417). The Crown of Aragon under Joan I supported the Avignon papacy (Clement VII), and these documents show the queen engaged in papal diplomacy alongside her husband.

- **The "fur" reference:** The document discusses conflicts between royal prerogatives (specifically debt collection from Jews) and local Aragonese *fueros* (regional law codes). - **"Guisar"/"guiatge":** Appears to relate to a *guiatge* (safe-conduct or protection) or debt arrangement. The Queen is asserting her right to collect debts despite local officials' resistance.

- **"Cortona" / "Girona":** The reading is uncertain. Given that the court regularly resided in Girona during this period, "Girona" is the more likely reading, though the paleography is difficult.

## HISTORICAL NOTES

### The Routier Crisis of 1387
Document 1 references "gentes d'armes d'estranya mao" (armed companies of foreign hand) - these were the notorious free companies (routiers/companyies) that plagued southern France and Iberia during the late 14th century. Following the Treaties of Brétigny (1360) and various truces in the Hundred Years' War, unemployed mercenaries formed companies that ravaged the countryside for plunder. Their incursion into Aragonese territories in late 1387 prompted defensive measures throughout the Queen's domains.

### Oloron (Olorpo)
All three documents are issued from "Olorpo" - Oloron-Sainte-Marie in Béarn. The court was apparently in this region in November 1387, likely due to the diplomatic activities mentioned (ambassadorship to France) and perhaps connected to the threat from mercenary companies operating in Gascony.

### Key Figures

1. **Violant de Bar** (c. 1365-1431): Queen consort of Aragon as wife of Joan I. Daughter of Robert I, Duke of Bar, and Marie of Valois. Active in governance, maintaining her own chancery and correspondence.

2. **Jaume Ferreter**: Regent of the procurator's office in the Queen's domains, responsible for administering her patrimony in the regions around Vilafranca del Penedès and Montblanc (Conca de Barberà).

3. **Ramon Alamany de Cervelló**: Chamberlain (Camarlenc) and ambassador of Joan I. The Cervelló family were prominent Catalan nobles with lands southwest of Barcelona. His dual role as chamberlain and ambassador indicates high trust.

4. **Bartolomeu Sirvent**: The Queen's secretary, responsible for the secretum (secret seal) documents. His name appears in all subscriptions.

### Fontrubia and Sant Martí
The order to evacuate Fontrubia's inhabitants to the castle of Sant Martí suggests a dispersed settlement being consolidated into a defensible position. The specific location needs further identification but likely lies in the Queen's patrimonial lands.

## 3. ENGLISH TRANSLATION

**[Salutation]**
Most dear and most beloved cousin, in order to satisfy our continuing desire that we have to know the state of your condition, we ask that you wish to notify us of this, for in knowing good news of it we receive consolation and very great pleasure.

**[Health notice]**
And [for you] wishing similarly to know of us, we certify to you that the lord King ever and my most dear husband, and we, and the Infantas our daughters, are all in good health and prosperity of our persons, thanks be to Our Lord God, which [health] may it please [Him] to grant to you and to us for a long time.

**[Political news]**
Besides this, most dear cousin, according to what we have already written to you by another letter given at Binéfar on the 4th day of the present month: the lord King has departed from Monzón with good accord from the Corts attendees, and has come to resist the foreign companies that are in the land. And now he is here in Barcelona, where he has been received with great joy and most solemnly, as befits [his station].

**[Military matters]**
And he wishes that the number of men-at-arms, pillarts [light cavalry/infantry], and crossbowmen that [were] granted to him in the General Corts that he was celebrating in Monzón by all his subjects—that is: for Catalonia, 400 men-at-arms, 400 pillarts, and 300 crossbowmen; and for the Kingdom of Aragon, 500 men-at-arms and 500 pillarts; and for the Kingdom of Valencia, 300 men-at-arms and 300 pillarts—now those of Catalonia have further granted another 400 men, which the said lord intends to have from foreign troops.

**[French alliance]**
[He intends] to request them from my lord Enric de Bar, my most dear brother, and the lord of Coucy, and Sir Johan de Sancerre, Marshal of France—who, he believes, will not fail in anything that touches his honor [and] will comply and serve willingly.

**[Embassy to France]**
And concerning this and certain other matters [being] treated and awaited with my most dear brother the King of France—who is at Toulouse—the lord King sends there his ambassadors, that is, the Viscount of Toda and others. Thus he hopes in my Lord God that the affairs of the lord King will succeed very well, to his honor and [the] good and good estate of his kingdoms and lands. And consequently we notify you of this, as one who loves the lord King cordially, and for [his] good fortune you will consequently have great pleasure.

**[Closing formula]**
And if any things please you that we can do, write back to us, for we will fulfill them with good heart. May the Holy Spirit be your guardian always.

**[Eschatocol]**
Given at Barcelona under the seal of my ring, on the 16th day of December of the year 1387.

The Queen.

[Chancery note:] The Lady Queen commanded me, Bartomeu Sirvent.

[Address notation:] Directed to the King of Navarre.

## 4. HISTORICAL NOTES

### Persons Mentioned:

1. **"lo senyor Rey" (Joan I of Aragon)**: King of Aragon 1387-1396; husband of Violant de Bar. Had recently succeeded his father Pere IV (d. January 1387).

2. **"les Infantes nostres filles"**: The daughters of Joan I and Violant de Bar at this time included Joana (b. 1375) and Violant (b. 1381).

3. **"Mossen Enric de Bar" (Henri de Bar)**: Brother of Queen Violant; son of Robert I, Duke of Bar. Important figure in French military affairs.

### Persons
1. **"Molt car frare" (Very dear brother):** This is the standard address from Violant de Bar to her brother-in-law **Martí, Duke of Montblanc** (1356–1410), later King Martí I "the Humane." Joan I's brother, he spent much of 1387–1392 in Sicily securing his son's inheritance.

2. **Mossèn Ximèn Pérez:** Almost certainly **Ximèn Pérez d'Arenós** or a related figure, a prominent Aragonese noble involved in Sardinian affairs. 3. **King of Cyprus:** This refers to **Peter II of Cyprus** (Pierre II de Lusignan), who died on 17 October 1382 — but the news may have just reached Barcelona, or this may refer to later succession disputes. - **Famagusta:** Key port city in Cyprus, contested between Genoa and various claimants after the Genoese seized it in 1373–74.
- **Sardinia:** The "fet de Sardenya" involves the ongoing conflicts between the Crown of Aragon and the Giudicato of Arborea.
- **Foggia (foga):** Port in Puglia; or possibly Focea (Phocaea) in Anatolia, a Genoese trading colony.

The date "M ccc lxxx e set" = 1387 falls at the **beginning** of the register's date range. This is plausible if we are near the start of the register. ## 3. ENGLISH TRANSLATION

**[To the] most high and most excellent prince, very dear and very beloved brother:**

Recently there have returned to the lord King, our very dear lord and husband, the Viscount of Roda, his Chamberlain, and N'Esperandeu Cardona, promoter of the affairs of his court, whom he had sent concerning certain matters. And by their report we have learned of the health and prosperity of your person, from which we have had very great pleasure and consolation.

And furthermore we have understood the terms in which you remained with them concerning the said matters—in particular, how regarding the matter of the agreements and alliances that exist between you and the lord King, you have delayed and suspended your response until your very dear uncles, the Dukes of Burgundy and Berry, should be with you. At this we are astonished.

Very dear brother, you understand that if a free and just response could and ought to be made—that is, to a thing proposed and agreed upon deliberately and with the accord and assent of your very dear uncles aforesaid—and since you likewise [consider it] expedient for the good and honor of your house and of your royal lineages, and consequently pleasing to us, [this] is no small [matter].

And yet we are not astonished at this, for we know with certainty that just as the lord King and we have cordial affection toward you and toward your house, so do you have [the same] toward him and toward us and toward his royal house. For the preservation and increase of which affection, the good observance of the other aforesaid agreements and alliances gives and will always give great cause and occasion among other things.

And thus we beseech you affectionately, very dear brother, that you should not give full place to neglecting those [agreements] and other observances, as you ought. And you may be certain that [the lord King] firmly hopes that regarding this matter, the lord King will have shortly your good response, with fulfillment of the things that you owe him by reason of the said agreements, and for the observance of those [agreements], and for the great and good bonds of kinship that exist between you both.

And if it pleases you [that there be] any things of which you should require [anything], say [it], for we will fulfill them with full willingness. And may the Holy Spirit always guard you, your very dear and very beloved brother.

**Given at Barcelona under our secret seal, on the 6th day of February of the year 1388. The Queen.**

*[Marginal note:]* Directed to the King of France.

*[Subscription:]* The Lady Queen commanded [this] to me, Bartolomeu Sirvent.

**Violant de Bar (c. 1365–1431)**: Queen consort of Aragon as wife of Joan I. Daughter of Robert I, Duke of Bar, and Marie of Valois, making her a member of the French royal house. Her mother was the sister of King Charles V of France, thus making Charles VI her first cousin. This refers to **Charles III of Navarre** ("Charles the Noble"), who succeeded his father Charles II in January 1387. The "declaration" likely refers to Charles III's formal declaration of obedience to Clement VII (Avignon pope) during the Western Schism, which the Cardinal de Luna, as Avignon's legate, had been promoting. The Crown of Aragon under Joan I also supported the Avignon papacy.

The term "cosín" (cousin) reflects the close dynastic ties between the houses of Aragon and Navarre.

### Queen Violant de Bar
Violant de Bar (1365–1431), daughter of Robert I, Duke of Bar, married Joan I of Aragon in 1380. She was an active political figure with her own chancery operations, as evidenced by this register (Curie Sigilli Secreti).
